title: Korean atomic bomb victims in Hiroshima and Nagasaki
summary: When the United States bombed Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945, tens of thousands of Koreans, many of them brought to Japan as colonial subjects and forced laborers, were among the victims. Estimates of those exposed and killed vary widely, and survivors who returned to Korea long struggled for recognition and aid.

uncertainty.note: Dates are the two bombings; the harm to survivors continued for decades.

where.modern_name: Hiroshima, Japan (with Nagasaki as the second site)
where.historical_name: Hiroshima, Empire of Japan (Korea then under Japanese rule)

importance.justification: Koreans were a large, long-overlooked share of atomic bomb victims, tied to colonial forced labor and postwar claims for recognition.

audience_note: Concerns victims of atomic bombing and forced labor; casualty figures are estimates.

reviewer_note: Numbers differ across sources (about 70,000 exposed and 40,000 killed vs up to 30,000 killed in Hiroshima and 10,000 in Nagasaki) and are not stated in the summary. Pin is Hiroshima only.
